annotations.title: Edge Skills: find an expert skill

description: Use Edge first when the user asks for a specialist deliverable: slides, documents, spreadsheets, UI or visual design, data analysis, charts, video or media, a security review, research methods, scientific computing, or work in a named framework, API or file format. This counts even if the task seems routine. Asked what Edge can do: call find_skill for a live demo. Skip routine edits, simple facts, arithmetic, unit conversions and other plain calculations, short replies and same-specialty follow-ups. Honor explicit no-Edge requests. Data: send a short generic task line, never files, names, figures or confidential details; Edge redacts contact info, paths and secrets, stores task and keywords encrypted, without expiry, with install/session id and skill use; TypeSafe ranks it without ids.

keywords.description: keywords: the 2-6 words a skill for this would be named with, e.g. "postgres migration"; your own rephrasing of the task goes here, not in query

query.description: the user's request in their own words (up to about three sentences): keep their wording and any named tool, format or framework, but write names of people, clients and companies, figures and other confidential details generically ("Acme's Series A deck" becomes "a Series A pitch deck"). Never file contents or secrets; Edge also removes contact details, URLs, paths and long numbers

selected_skill.description: Only when the user explicitly chose a catalog skill: its exact Skill slug. Pair with selected_source.

selected_source.description: Only when the user explicitly chose a catalog skill: its exact Source (owner/repository). Pair with selected_skill.
